text: Great art Thou, O Lord, and greatly to be praised; great is Thy power, and Thy wisdom infinite.
My faith, Lord, shall call on Thee, which Thou hast given me, wherewith Thou hast inspired me, through the Incarnation of Thy Son, through the ministry of the Preacher.
zh: 主啊，我的信仰将呼求祢，祢已赐给我，祢借祢的儿子的道成肉身，通过传道者的事工，启发了我。
chunks: My faith, Lord, shall call on Thee,
through the Incarnation of Thy Son,
through the ministry of the Preacher.

text: Do the heaven and earth then contain Thee, since Thou fillest them? or dost Thou fill them and yet overflow, since they do not contain Thee?
zh: 既然你充满了天地，那么天地还能容纳你吗？还是你充满了它们却溢出了，因为它们并不含有你？
chunks: Do the heaven and earth then contain Thee,
since they do not contain Thee?

text: For who is Lord but the Lord? or who is God save our God?
zh: 因为除了主以外谁是主呢？或者除了我们的神之外，谁是神呢？
chunks: but the Lord? or who is God save our God?

text: Oh! that I might repose on Thee!
zh: 哦！使我可以安息在你身上！

text: Oh! for Thy mercies' sake, tell me, O Lord my God, what Thou art unto me.
zh: 哦！主啊我的神啊，求你因你的怜悯告诉我，你对我来说意味着什么。

text: Let me die--lest I die--only let me see Thy face.
zh: 让我死吧——免得我死——只让我看看你的脸。

text: I believe, and therefore do I speak.
zh: 我相信，因此我说话。

text: Thou too, perhaps, despisest me, yet wilt Thou return and have compassion upon me.
For they, with a heaven-taught affection, willingly gave me what they abounded with from Thee.
zh: 因为他们怀着天赐的情感，心甘情愿地把从你那里得到的丰富的东西给了我。
chunks: willingly gave me what they abounded

text: Thus, little by little, I became conscious where I was; and to have a wish to express my wishes to those who could content them, and I could not; for the wishes were within me, and they without; nor could they by any sense of theirs enter within my spirit.
chunks: Thus, little by little, I became conscious where I was;
and to have a wish to express my wishes to those
who could content them, and I could not;
for the wishes were within me, and they without;
nor could they by any sense of theirs enter within my spirit.

text: For this have I none to tell me, neither father nor mother, nor experience of others, nor mine own memory.
zh: 因为这一点我没有人可以告诉我，无论是父亲还是母亲，也没有别人的经验，也没有我自己的记忆。

text: For they had no way to pass away, unless Thou upheldest them.
zh: 因为除非你扶持他们，否则他们无法消逝。

text: Let him rejoice even thus! and be content rather by not discovering to discover Thee, than by discovering not to discover Thee.
zh: 即便如此，也让他高兴吧！与其满足于不去发现你，不如去发现不去发现你。
chunks: by not discovering to discover Thee,

text: I could not understand reproof, custom and reason forbade me to be reproved.
zh: 我无法理解责备，习俗和理由禁止我受到责备。

text: Mothers and nurses tell you that they allay these things by I know not what remedies.
zh: 母亲和护士告诉你，他们通过我不知道什么补救措施来缓解这些问题。
chunks: that they allay these things by I know not what remedies.

text: For no less than that which I spent in my mother's womb, is it hid from me in the shadows of forgetfulness.
zh: 因为它就像我在母亲子宫里度过的一样，被隐藏在遗忘的阴影中。

text: This I remember; and have since observed how I learned to speak.
I was put to school to get learning, in which I (poor wretch) knew not what use there was; and yet, if idle in learning, I was beaten.
zh: 我被送去学校学习，我（可怜的家伙）不知道学习有什么用；然而，如果我闲于学习，我就会被打败。
chunks: in which I (poor wretch) knew not what use there was;

text: And yet we sinned, in writing or reading or studying less than was exacted of us.
zh: 然而，我们在写作、阅读或学习方面却犯了罪，比我们所要求的要少。

text: Yet those who give these shows are in such esteem, that almost all wish the same for their children, and yet are very willing that they should be beaten, if those very games detain them from the studies, whereby they would have them attain to be the givers of them.
chunks: Yet those who give these shows are
in such esteem, that almost all wish the same
for their children, and yet are very willing that they should be beaten,
if those very games detain them from the studies,
whereby they would have them attain to be the givers of them.

text: For it was her earnest care that Thou my God, rather than he, shouldest be my father; and in this Thou didst aid her to prevail over her husband, whom she, the better, obeyed, therein also obeying Thee, who hast so commanded.
zh: 因为她热切地希望你，我的上帝，而不是他，成为我的父亲。在这一点上，你帮助她战胜了她的丈夫，她服从了丈夫，也服从了你的命令。
chunks: For it was her earnest care
that Thou my God, rather than he, shouldest be my father;
and in this Thou didst aid her
to prevail over her husband, whom she, the better, obeyed,
therein also obeying Thee, who hast so commanded.

text: I loved not study, and hated to be forced to it.
zh: 我不喜欢学习，也讨厌被迫学习。

text: So by those who did not well, Thou didst well for me; and by my own sin Thou didst justly punish me.
zh: 因此，那些做得不好的人，你却为我做得很好；你因我自己的罪孽而公正地惩罚了我。
chunks: and by my own sin Thou didst justly punish me.

text: For what more miserable than a miserable being who commiserates not himself; weeping the death of Dido for love to Aeneas, but weeping not his own death for want of love to Thee, O God.
zh: 还有什么比一个不同情自己的可怜人更悲惨的呢？上帝啊，他为狄多的死而哭泣，是因为他对埃涅阿斯的爱，但他自己的死，却不是因为缺乏对你的爱而哭泣。
chunks: For what more miserable than a miserable being
who commiserates not himself; weeping the death
of Dido for love to Aeneas,
but weeping not his own death
for want of love to Thee, O God.

text: Not so, not so.
For if I question them whether it be true that Aeneas came on a time to Carthage, as the poet tells, the less learned will reply that they know not, the more learned that he never did.
zh: 因为如果我问他们，埃涅阿斯是否真的像诗人所说的那样，在某个时间来到了迦太基，学识较少的人会回答说他们不知道，而学识较多的人会回答说他从未这样做过。

that they know not, the more learned

zh: 荷马也奇怪地编织了类似的小说，而且是最甜蜜的虚荣，但他对我孩子气的口味来说是苦涩的。
chunks: Homer also curiously wove the like fictions,

text: No doubt, then, that a free curiosity has more force in our learning these things, than a frightful enforcement.
zh: 那么，毫无疑问，自由的好奇心比可怕的强制力更能帮助我们学习这些东西。
chunks: that a free curiosity has more force

text: But woe is thee, thou torrent of human custom!
zh: 但你有祸了，你这人类习俗的洪流！

text: Viewing a picture, where the tale was drawn, Of Jove's descending in a golden shower To Danae's lap a woman to beguile.
zh: 观看故事的画作，朱庇特在金色的雨中降临到达那厄的膝上，迷惑一个女人。
chunks: Of Jove's descending in a golden shower

text: Bear with me, my God, while I say somewhat of my wit, Thy gift, and on what dotages I wasted it.
zh: 请容忍我，我的上帝，让我谈谈我的智慧，你的天赋，以及我在什么时候浪费了它。
chunks: and on what dotages I wasted it.

text: For in more ways than one do men sacrifice to the rebellious angels.
zh: 因为人们以多种方式向叛逆的天使做出牺牲。
chunks: than one do men sacrifice to the rebellious angels.

text: So then in lustful, that is, in darkened affections, is the true distance from Thy face.
zh: 因此，在贪欲中，即在黑暗的情感中，才是与你面容真正的距离。

text: This was the world at whose gate unhappy I lay in my boyhood; this the stage where I had feared more to commit a barbarism, than having committed one, to envy those who had not.
chunks: This was the world at whose gate unhappy I lay
in my boyhood; this the stage
to commit a barbarism, than having committed one,
to envy those who had not.

text: And what could I so ill endure, or, when I detected it, upbraided I so fiercely, as that I was doing to others? and for which if, detected, I was upbraided, I chose rather to quarrel than to yield.
zh: 我能如此难以忍受，或者当我发现这一点时，如此严厉地斥责我，就像我对别人所做的那样吗？如果我被发现为此受到责备，我宁愿争吵也不愿屈服。
chunks: And what could I so ill endure, or,
when I detected it, upbraided I so fiercely,
as that I was doing to others? and for
which if, detected, I was upbraided,
I chose rather to quarrel than to yield.

text: But all are gifts of my God: it was not I who gave them me; and good these are, and these together are myself.
zh: 但一切都是上帝的恩赐：不是我把它们给了我；而是我把它们给了我。这些都是好的，这些加起来就是我自己。
chunks: But all are gifts of my God:

text: For I even burnt in my youth heretofore, to be satiated in things below; and I dared to grow wild again, with these various and shadowy loves: my beauty consumed away, and I stank in Thine eyes; pleasing myself, and desirous to please in the eyes of men.
chunks: For I even burnt in my youth heretofore,
to be satiated in things below; and I dared to grow wild again,
with these various and shadowy loves: my beauty consumed away,
and I stank in Thine eyes; pleasing myself, and desirous

text: O Lord: who this way formest the offspring of this our death, being able with a gentle hand to blunt the thorns which were excluded from Thy paradise?
zh: 主啊：谁以这种方式形成了我们死亡的后代，能够用温柔的手削掉那些被排除在你天堂之外的荆棘？
chunks: O Lord: who this way formest the offspring
of this our death, being able
which were excluded from Thy paradise?

text: And to what purpose? that whosoever reads this, may think out of what depths we are to cry unto Thee.
zh: 目的是什么？凡读到此文的人，都会想到我们该向你呼求的深渊。
chunks: out of what depths we are

text: Thy temple, and the foundation of Thy holy habitation, whereas my father was as yet but a Catechumen, and that but recently.
zh: 你的圣殿，你神圣居所的根基，而我父亲还只是一个慕道者，而且是最近才这样。

text: For she wished, and I remember in private with great anxiety warned me, "not to commit fornication; but especially never to defile another man's wife.
zh: 因为她希望——我记得私下里非常焦虑地警告过我——“不要犯奸淫；尤其是不要玷污别人的妻子。

zh: 看哪，我与多少同伴一起走过巴比伦的街道，并在其中打滚，仿佛在香料和珍贵香膏的床上打滚。

To shake and rob this, some lewd young fellows of us went, late one night (having according to our pestilent custom prolonged our sports in the streets till then), and took huge loads, not for our eating, but to fling to the very hogs, having only tasted them.

text: For there is an attractiveness in beautiful bodies, in gold and silver, and all things; and in bodily touch, sympathy hath much influence, and each other sense hath his proper object answerably tempered.
zh: 因为美丽的身体、金银以及一切事物都具有吸引力。在身体接触中，同情心具有很大的影响力，彼此的感觉都得到了适当的调和。
chunks: in beautiful bodies, in gold and silver,
and all things; and in bodily touch,
and each other sense hath his proper object answerably tempered.

zh: 因为这些低等的事物也有它们的乐趣，但不像我的上帝，他创造了万物；因为义人喜悦他；心里正直的人也以他为喜乐。

zh: 那么，在我十六岁的时候，我如此爱你，你偷窃了我的东西，你黑暗的行为，我到底做了什么？
chunks: in that sixteenth year of my age?

text: For so doth pride imitate exaltedness; whereas Thou alone art God exalted over all.
zh: 因为骄傲就是如此模仿崇高；而唯独你才是被高举于万有之上的神。
chunks: For so doth pride imitate exaltedness;
whereas Thou alone art God exalted

text: Yea, sloth would fain be at rest; but what stable rest besides the Lord?
zh: 是的，树懒很想休息；但除了主以外，还有什么安息呢？
chunks: but what stable rest besides the Lord?

text: Fear startles at things unwonted and sudden, which endangers things beloved, and takes forethought for their safety; but to Thee what unwonted or sudden, or who separateth from Thee what Thou lovest?
zh: 恐惧会因不寻常和突然的事情而受到惊吓，这会危及所爱的人，并为他们的安全而预先考虑；但对你来说，什么是不寻常的或突然的，或者是谁将你所爱的东西与你分开呢？

but to Thee what unwonted or sudden, or who separateth

zh: 我是否希望即使是偷偷地做违反你的法律的事，因为通过权力我不能，这样作为一个囚犯，我就可以模仿一种有缺陷的自由，做我不允许的事情而不受惩罚，这是你全能的黑暗肖像？

Yet alone I had not done it: such was I then, I remember, alone I had never done it.
zh: 然而我一个人还没有做到这一点：我记得当时我就是这样，一个人从来没有做到过。
chunks: Yet alone I had not done it:

zh: 那么为什么我如此高兴而不是我一个人做的呢？

text: Foul is it: I hate to think on it, to look on it.
zh: 这很糟糕：我讨厌去想它，不愿意看着它。

text: I loved not yet, yet I loved to love, and out of a deep-seated want, I hated myself for wanting not.
zh: 我还没有爱过，但我喜欢去爱，出于一种根深蒂固的渴望，我恨自己不想要。
chunks: I hated myself for wanting not.

text: I fell headlong then into the love wherein I longed to be ensnared.
zh: 于是我一头扎进了我渴望陷入的爱情之中。
chunks: into the love wherein I longed to be ensnared.

text: But what sort of compassion is this for feigned and scenical passions? for the auditor is not called on to relieve, but only to grieve: and he applauds the actor of these fictions the more, the more he grieves.
zh: 但这对于虚假的、风景如画的激情来说是一种什么样的同情心呢？因为审计师不是被要求去缓解的，而只是去悲伤的：他越是为这些虚构的演员鼓掌，他就越悲伤。

for feigned and scenical passions? for the auditor is not called

of these fictions the more, the more he grieves.

and the loss of some miserable felicity.

zh: 那么，还有什么比“颠覆者”更贴切的称呼呢？自己首先败坏，全然败坏，邪灵暗中戏弄、引诱他们，自己则乐于嘲笑、迷惑别人。
